wa_pit_the_2.blurb: A tight cluster of thirteen boulders in the Treasury zone of the Skykomish Valley, in the Central-West Cascades within reach of Seattle. It sits near 3,700 feet, tucked directly above and behind the Top Sail boulder, so you reach it by scrambling up from that block. All of it is bouldering. The grades run low to middle, with most problems between V1 and V3, plus a handful of much harder lines around V6 for climbers looking for a stiffer test. A small, compact spot that pairs well with the neighbouring boulders in the same field.

wa_rabbit_hole.blurb: A small, steep crag in the Salal Point group on Mt Washington, off the Exit 38 corridor near North Bend. Routes are short, around 20 metres, with roofs, thin technical faces, stemming and mantles; the hard moves tend to be bouldery and followed by decent rests. Twelve of the thirteen lines are sport and one is trad, graded roughly 5.10d to 5.12, with 5.11 the bulk of it. The wall stays in shade for most of the day, which makes it a sensible pick when it is hot. Find it by walking just beyond the upper Valley View East crag and stepping over a small fallen tree.

wa_slingblade_boulder.blurb: One of the roadside blocks in the Pitless Avocado cluster in Tumwater Canyon, near Leavenworth. It lies on the opposite side of the road from the Hueco Crimper Boulder, about fifty yards further east. Thirteen problems, all bouldering, cover a very wide range: a couple of easy warm-ups, a solid middle group from V3 to V6, and a block of seriously hard sit-start and variation lines from V10 up into the V13 range. The namesake line is the best-known problem here and a popular tick for strong boulderers.

wa_hot_rock.blurb: A section of the main wall at Calendar Butte, beside the Walker Valley riding area in northwest Washington. This is the sunniest stretch of the cliff, with no trees overhead, so it suits clear, cold days and gets very warm by mid-morning in summer. Thirteen routes: eleven sport and two trad, from about 5.8 up to 5.13, with the bulk of them falling in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. A few of the longer lines take two pitches. Walk to the main wall and follow the trail over the boulders until you can cut up left to the platform at the base.

wa_4_gold_wall.blurb: A wall within Ozone, the roadside cliff band on the Washington shore of the Columbia Gorge. It holds thirteen routes, a near-even mix of trad (seven) and sport (six), from about 5.7 to 5.11. The grades are weighted to the middle: several 5.9s and 5.10s, a few easier leads and a pair of 5.11s. It works well for climbers stepping up from moderates, and the broader Ozone cliff sees steady traffic whenever the rock is dry, so expect company.
